heroHeadline: ISAACMAN "EXTREMELY CONFIDENT" ARTEMIS III LAUNCHES IN 2027, DETAILS 3-LAUNCH ORDER; SLS BOOSTER NOSE CONES ARRIVE AT VAB
heroSubtitle: Aug 14: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said he is "extremely confident" Artemis III will launch in 2027, detailing the mission's three-launch sequence for the first time: Blue Origin's New Glenn flies first carrying a Blue Moon Mark 2 test lander with life-support and crew-habitation areas installed, followed days later by the SLS rocket with Orion, and then SpaceX's Starship Version 3 with a docking adapter. Isaacman, who recently toured Blue Origin's assembly line, called SpaceX's rising launch cadence "critical," citing a planned early-September flight and roughly biweekly launches through year-end. HARDWARE: The aerodynamic nose cones for the twin Artemis III SLS solid rocket boosters arrived at Kennedy Space Center's Vehicle Assembly Building Aug 13, continuing stacking that remains roughly four months ahead of the equivalent point in the Artemis II campaign; the Orion crew and service modules were joined July 30 and all four RS-25 core-stage engines are on site. MOON BASE: Four commercial lunar landers — Blue Origin, Firefly Aerospace, Intuitive Machines, and Voyager Technologies — cleared major testing milestones by August 4. ARCHITECTURE: NASA and Northrop Grumman confirmed Aug 6 that the cancelled Gateway's HALO module will be reused across three Lunar Infrastructure Demo missions (LID-1/2/3) feeding Moon Base Phase I, and Canada said the same day it will redirect its Canadarm3 investment from the shelved Gateway toward Artemis lunar-surface operations. SETBACK: Blue Origin traced its May 28 New Glenn static-fire explosion to a BE-4 engine oxygen valve; the Blue Moon Mark 1 cargo lander needed for Moon Base I's rover delivery has slipped from late summer 2026 to Q1 2027. Artemis Accords stand at 70 signatory nations.
